## PCE帶動美債先漲，油價反彈收斂漲幅

週四美債先因PCE通膨低於市場擔憂而上漲，之後荷莫茲海峽附近一艘貨船遇襲、數艘船隻折返，油價由跌轉漲，債券漲幅也隨之收斂。5月整體PCE月增幅低於預期，核心則符合預估，曾帶動30年期殖利率降至4.82%、創3月以來最低；收盤回到4.86%，與前一天持平。2年期仍保留2個基點跌幅，收在4.09%。

盤中反轉使結果有別於週三的全面上漲。10年期實質殖利率下降4個基點至2.19%，損益兩平通膨率卻上升3個基點至2.21%，名目殖利率因此僅下降1個基點至4.40%。通膨沒有出現原先擔憂的超預期升幅，投資人接受較低的實質報酬；船運事件則重新提高對能源漲價的防備。

美國經濟仍未顯示政策可以迅速轉鬆。初領失業救濟金人數下降、第1季成長上修，排除運輸的訂單也增加，交換市場只小幅調降Fed升息定價。7年期標售需求良好，有助支撐美債。信用市場則出現更具體的分歧：SpaceX新券利差擴大，Braskem在債權人否決重整方案後，聲請緊急司法保護。

## 通膨減輕立即升息壓力，經濟活動仍有支撐

5月PCE物價月增0.4%，低於調查中位數0.5%；核心月增0.3%，符合預期。整體年增率仍加速至4.1%，核心升至3.4%、創2023年以來最高。這份資料比原先擔憂的好，通膨水準卻不低。交換市場對12月以前升息的定價，由週三收盤約36個基點降至34個基點，7月升息機率則降至約三分之一。

勞動與需求資料限制了利率預期進一步下修。初領失業救濟金人數由修正後22.7萬降至21.5萬，續領人數則由180.0萬升至182.1萬。耐久財訂單在4月大增8.5%後，5月下降4.5%，主要受運輸設備下滑14.0%拖累；排除運輸後，訂單反而增加1.3%。第1季GDP年化成長上修至2.1%。堪薩斯市Fed綜合指數由8升至11，生產、訂單與就業改善，兩項主要價格指數則達2022年以來最高。

芝加哥Fed總裁Austan Goolsbee認為通膨報告部分內容令人鼓舞，但核心仍太高，而且方向不對。紐約Fed總裁John Williams也表示，通膨無疑偏高，目前政策有利於把它帶回目標。前一週會議中，19位決策者有9位預測今年至少升息一次。資料讓官員有空間再觀察，尚不足以消除通膨疑慮。

美債殖利率一度降至至少一週低點，油價反彈後再度回升。2及5年期收盤各下降2個基點，至4.09%及4.15%；10年期下降1個基點至4.40%。30年期持平，使曲線小幅陡峭化，2年與10年期利差擴大1個基點至31，2年與30年期擴大2個基點至77。

實質殖利率則各天期都下降。5年期下跌6個基點至1.92%，7年期下跌4個基點至2.05%，20與30年期各下跌2個基點，至2.51%及2.69%。10年期增加的通膨補償，抵銷了名目債券大部分漲幅。能源打斷了行情，卻沒有扭轉當天實質殖利率下降的方向。

財政部標售$440億7年期公債，得標殖利率4.260%，與美東13:00截止前的交易水準一致。發行公告後，參考殖利率曾高達4.40%，但經過債市上漲，標售需求仍良好。本輪固定利率券供給至此結束，下一筆是7月7日3年期標售。

國庫券也順利消化大額供給。$700億28天期最高得標利率3.610%，投標倍數2.74；間接投標人取得競爭性得標額的65.14%，交易商31.23%，直接投標人3.63%。$750億56天期得標利率3.660%，投標倍數2.79，間接、交易商及直接投標人分別取得69.52%、27.85%與2.62%。兩券均於6月30日交割。次級市場4及8週期息票等值殖利率上升6與2個基點，至3.68%及3.74%；6週期持平於3.69%，其他短天期漲跌不一，壓力主要集中在當天標售的天期。

## SpaceX利差擴大，Braskem轉向法院

SpaceX完成$250億首筆發債兩天後，新券在次級市場走弱。10年期利差來到美債加157個基點，比發行時140個基點擴大17個基點。大型交易完成後，投資人對公司龐大支出及距離自由現金流仍有相當時間的疑慮，繼續反映在價格上。

交易商也開始積極報價5年期SpaceX信用違約交換。一筆報價中間值約為每年125.5個基點，相當於為$1,000萬債務買保護，每年支付約$12.55萬；評級相近的Intel約為64個基點。即使SpaceX有投資級評等與充裕流動性，資本密集、治理權力集中及未來融資需求仍需要額外補償。CDS數字是其中一筆市場報價，現券利差擴大則提供另一個實際交易觀察。

Braskem的協商進一步走向法律程序。債權人否決延長天期、降低票息及提供寬限期的庭外方案後，公司聲請緊急司法保護。其金融債務約$95億，2026年7月至2027年12月約有$37億本息須支付，股價下跌逾10%。重整尚待完成，股東支持、擔保品與債權順位將成為後續程序核心。

印尼大型鎳冶煉商Gunbuster Nickel Industry，則在礦石短缺與金屬價格疲弱之際，進入法院命令的暫時停止償債程序。印尼在主要由中國資金與技術支持的擴產後，已供應全球逾60%的鎳。國家產量居主導地位，個別項目仍可能因成本、原料與融資承壓，最終債權回收尚未確定。

Strategy的永久特別股STRC則在比特幣跌破$6萬、買盤退縮後，從$100發行價跌至約$75。這項證券對公司比特幣沒有請求權，沒有到期日，股息也可由董事會調降或暫停；Strategy本身評級為B−。支撐持續買入比特幣的融資工具變得更昂貴，特別股投資人承擔的順位也低於一般債權。

### 銀行融資與信評制度各有變化

橫濱金融集團首次發行優先債，規模¥120億、天期3年，定價為日債加27個基點。最終訂單約為發行額1.2倍，買家包括壽險、投資顧問及信託銀行。日本央行升息至1%後，存款競爭加劇，仍有放款需求的區域銀行開始增加批發融資。這次發行打開了管道，但訂單並不充裕。

中國監理機關要求信評公司檢視最高評等過度集中的情況，並把發行利差相對同類公債的水準，納入評估指標之一。利差超過200個基點的發行人，可能面臨失去AAA評級的風險，但仍須考慮其他因素。第1季末逾6,000家發行人中，27%為AAA，另32%為AA+。評級若能拉開差距，有助投資人辨別風險，也可能提高部分長期享有最高本地評等借款人的成本。

美國FDIC則提議，把部分保費評估架構的資產門檻由$100億提高至$300億。存款保險基金準備率為1.43%，高於法定最低1.35%，也是數十年來最高。降低保費可稍微增加受影響銀行的保留盈餘，但提案尚未定案，基金承擔損失的義務也未改變。

與這些個別發展相比，信用ETF波動很小。LQD上漲0.08%，HYG上漲0.04%，JNK上漲0.09%。次級利差、法律狀態與資本結構，比接近持平的基金報酬，更能說明當天信用風險的變化。

## 日本長債需求轉弱，投資計畫擴大融資疑問

日本20年期公債投標倍數降至2.97，為2025年5月以來最低，也低於12個月平均。尾差為1月以來最大，最低得標價格明顯低於標售前估計。壽險與全球資產管理機構減少超長債曝險後，需求似乎主要來自銀行。這個結果接續壽險5月賣出日債的情況，使市場更擔心曲線重新陡峭化。

首相高市早苗的策略也帶來長期融資問題。計畫在14年間促成逾¥370兆、約合$2.3兆公共與民間投資，涵蓋AI、半導體等領域。政府估計每年財政支出約¥10兆，可能搭配過渡性債券、稅收與支出節省籌資。整體投資目標並非全數公共債務，但發債與債務比率暫時上升，可能早於預期成長效益。

日本央行委員田村直樹以每隔數月升息25個基點、朝約2%中性利率前進，作為自己的基本情境；央行前一週才升至1%。植田和男再次強調，後續須視成長與通膨。日圓持續偏弱，輸入性物價壓力仍在。長債投標偏弱、潛在供給與進一步升息，同時影響國內投資人的存續期間選擇。

東京CPI於6月26日日本時間8:30、紐約收盤後公布。排除生鮮食品的物價年增1.6%，再排除能源則增1.9%；主要指標8個月來首次加速，水費在補貼結束後上升是主因。這份資料更新的是接下來亞洲交易時段的通膨判斷，週四市場先前已在反映標售與政策消息。

歐洲在油價先前大跌後，政策展望變得較不激進。Oxford Economics取消6月之後再升息一次的預測，其他機構也減少預期次數，市場仍反映今年再升1碼。Isabel Schnabel與Emmanuel Moulin維持通膨警戒，不過Moulin認為最近一次升息溫和，也指出油價已低於最新預測的假設。討論逐漸轉向ECB可以暫停多久。

英國10年期公債殖利率此前已降至約4.7%、創3月中旬以來最低，整體英債報酬也在政治不確定性中升至3個月高點。進口能源成本下降有助這波回升。週四油價反彈使部分支撐受到考驗，但此前原油的大幅下跌仍在。

中國則新增隔夜逆回購工具，搭配自2025年5月維持1.4%的7天期政策利率。人民銀行因而能更直接調節隔夜資金、抑制貨幣市場波動。第2季動能轉弱之際，交易員從制度變動讀出寬鬆傾向，與日本持續正常化的方向不同。

## 產油國失去部分支撐，中國推介歐元主權債

原油6月下跌期間，非洲產油國美元債落後大盤。剛果共和國境外債跌逾2%，安哥拉、喀麥隆、加彭與奈及利亞跌逾1%，同時新興市場平均上漲0.5%。安哥拉2048年券殖利率由6月初低點上升逾60個基點至9.94%；剛果2036年券升約66個基點至10.01%，奈及利亞2034年券升33個基點至7.33%。

中國需求疲弱，使部分安哥拉原油品級跌至逾10年低價，也降低對剛果石油的購買意願。奈及利亞因Dangote煉油廠帶動本地需求，加上先前匯市改革提高韌性，表現較佳。週四供給安全溢價回升有利油價，一個月的大幅跌勢仍影響出口收入與融資前景。

中國財政部正在推介最高€50億、5、8及12年期債券，初始指引分別為中間交換利率加15、22及33個基點。這可能成為中國最大歐元主權發行；7個月前一筆€40億交易，曾吸引逾€1,000億訂單。提早回到市場，是希望在歐洲可能出現更多通膨與利率壓力前，取得有利融資。這些仍是推介條件，最終定價尚待完成。

中國也在G20共同框架下，呼籲採取法律與技術措施，限制債券持有人的積極訴訟。衣索比亞$10億違約債的協商，未能達成債券持有人小組與中國共同領導的官方債權人都可接受的條件，投資人已開始提告。負擔分攤、執行與優先債權人待遇仍是協商核心，官方減債尚未促成持久的私人債權人和解。

匈牙利的制度整合前景則吸引買盤。10年期殖利率降至5.16%，與英債差距不到0.5個百分點，3月溢價曾達2.6個百分點；對德國利差收窄至2.3個百分點，約為3個月前的一半。可取得逾€160億先前凍結的歐盟援助，以及在2030年前符合加入歐元條件的承諾，支持了這波走勢，儘管匈牙利評級較低。

菲律賓10年期殖利率在6月15日美伊臨時協議後下跌約50個基點，是新興亞洲最強反彈；先前衝突升級至6月12日期間，卻已上升157個基點。BSP把利率升至4.75%，並將2026年通膨預測提高至6.4%，超過2%至4%目標；一項預測認為還會再升3次、每次25個基點，至5.50%。反彈仍容易受到物價、披索與聖嬰現象供給風險影響。

印尼為管理約$9,000億國有資產的Danantara籌資，加入具爭議性的法律保障。新金融部門法使購買該基金債券免受刑事、民事及稅務調查，並禁止把債券紀錄用於稅務評估或法庭證據。印尼稅收約占GDP的10%，措施可能吸引未申報資金回流，支應不計入表面預算赤字的項目；可追溯性降低，也為投資人帶來治理與聲譽疑問。

Banxico維持6.50%，並暗示較長時間暫停調整，即使墨西哥整體通膨較低、成長疲弱。第1季GDP萎縮0.6%，2026年成長預測由1.6%下修至1.1%，但核心通膨持續及美國政策影響，使理事會仍強調物價上行風險。披索在決策後保持穩定。廣泛新興市場美元債方面，EMB僅跌0.01%，美元當日小幅走低減輕眼前壓力，卻未扭轉一個月的升值。

## 晶片股回升，荷莫茲事件推高油價

Micron展望恢復市場對AI硬體的信心，帶動半導體指數上漲3.59%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.75%。Apple調高Mac、iPad與家庭裝置價格後，股價下跌6.1%；S&P 500同日幾乎持平、小跌0.01%。VIX上升1.40%至18.89，市場強弱仍集中在不同個股。

集中程度已相當高。截至週三，8檔基礎建設相關股票，貢獻S&P 500年初以來7.5%漲幅中的近三分之二；半導體指數即使週二下跌7.9%，2026年仍上漲約93%。少數公司的投資與融資決策，因而對整體市場有異常大的影響。

船隻遇襲後，WTI由早盤下跌轉為收漲2.25%、報$71.92，布蘭特上漲2.06%至$75.26。事件前兩者都曾接近戰前價格，一週仍下跌約6%，一個月WTI跌逾25%、布蘭特跌逾27%。油價重新加入部分地緣政治溢價，與美債通膨補償上升一致，但仍保留此前大部分能源成本緩解。

美元指數下降0.18%至101.43，一週及一個月仍分別上升0.58%與2.12%。黃金上漲1.01%至$4,030.50，一週及一個月則仍下跌4.58%與10.85%。黃金與原油回應船運不確定性，債券投資人同時保留了早盤實質殖利率下降的部分成果。

## 接續看通膨預期與季底供給

6月26日美東時間10:00，將公布密西根大學消費者調查終值及紐約Fed多變量核心趨勢通膨指標。密大初值為信心48.9、1年通膨預期4.6%、長期預期3.4%。這些更新將提供持續性價格壓力的觀察，與週四優於擔憂的PCE及油價反彈對照。

日本6月26日約12:35標售約¥4.1兆3個月期國庫券，6月30日標售約¥2.8兆2年期公債，7月2日另有約¥2.6兆新10年期券。結果將顯示需求偏弱是否集中在超長端。6月30日活動資料及7月1日短觀調查，也會更新日本央行下一步所參考的投資與價格預期。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Oil Rebound Trims the Treasury Rally After PCE Relief

Treasuries pared an early rally Thursday after a cargo ship was struck near the Strait of Hormuz and several vessels turned back, reversing a decline in oil. Inflation data had first drawn buyers into bonds: May headline PCE rose less than forecast and core prices matched estimates. The 30-year yield briefly reached 4.82%, its lowest since March, before returning to 4.86%, unchanged on the day. The two-year retained a 2-basis-point decline to 4.09%.

The reversal left a different result from Wednesday's broad rally. Ten-year real yields fell 4 basis points to 2.19%, but breakeven inflation rose 3 to 2.21%, limiting the nominal yield's decline to 1 basis point, at 4.40%. Investors reduced the real return they required after the feared inflation overshoot failed to appear, while the shipping incident restored some demand for protection against higher energy prices.

The US economy offered little reason to expect rapid policy relief. Initial claims fell, first-quarter growth was revised higher and orders excluding transportation increased. Swaps trimmed expected Fed tightening only slightly. A well-received seven-year auction supported Treasuries, while credit investors found more to differentiate among borrowers: SpaceX's newly issued bonds widened against benchmarks, and Braskem sought emergency court protection after creditors rejected its restructuring proposal.

## Inflation Eases Hike Urgency, but Activity Holds Up

May's PCE price index increased 0.4% monthly against a 0.5% median forecast; core rose 0.3%, as expected. Annual headline inflation accelerated to 4.1% and core to 3.4%, the highest core reading since 2023. The release was better than feared without being low. Swaps reduced the tightening priced through December to about 34 basis points from roughly 36 at Wednesday's close, and the implied chance of a July increase fell to around one in three.

Labor and demand figures limited the case for a larger change. Initial unemployment claims dropped to 215,000 from a revised 227,000, although insured unemployment increased to 1.821 million from 1.800 million. Durable-goods orders fell 4.5% after April's 8.5% jump, led by a 14.0% decline in transportation equipment; excluding transportation, orders grew 1.3%. First-quarter GDP was revised to a 2.1% annualized gain. The Kansas City Fed composite rose to 11 from 8, with stronger production, orders and employment, while both main price indexes reached their highest levels since 2022.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee found parts of the inflation report encouraging but said core inflation remained too high and was moving in the wrong direction. New York Fed President John Williams called inflation unquestionably elevated and said policy was well positioned to bring it back to target. Nine of 19 policymakers had projected at least one increase this year at the previous week's meeting. The data gave officials room to wait for more evidence, rather than a reason to abandon that concern.

Yields initially fell to their lowest levels in at least a week. Oil's subsequent rebound pulled them away from the lows, leaving the two- and five-year yields down 2 basis points, at 4.09% and 4.15%, and the 10-year down 1 at 4.40%. The unchanged long bond meant the curve steepened modestly: 2s10s widened 1 basis point to 31 and 2s30s widened 2 to 77.

Real yields still declined across maturities. The five-year fell 6 basis points to 1.92%, the seven-year dropped 4 to 2.05%, and the 20- and 30-year each eased 2, to 2.51% and 2.69%. At 10 years, renewed inflation compensation offset most of that benefit to the nominal bond. Energy had interrupted the rally without reversing the day's decline in real yields.

Treasury sold $44 billion of seven-year notes at 4.260%, matching the level traded immediately before the 13:00 ET deadline. The indicated yield had been as high as 4.40% after the auction was announced, yet demand was good after the rally. The sale completed the fixed-rate auction calendar until the July 7 three-year offering.

Bills also cleared in size. The $70 billion 28-day sale stopped at 3.610% with 2.74 bid-to-cover. Indirect bidders took 65.14% of competitive awards, dealers 31.23% and direct bidders 3.63%. The $75 billion 56-day sale stopped at 3.660% with 2.79 cover; indirect, dealer and direct shares were 69.52%, 27.85% and 2.62%. Both settle June 30. Secondary four- and eight-week coupon-equivalent yields rose 6 and 2 basis points, to 3.68% and 3.74%, while six-week yields held at 3.69% and other short maturities were mixed. The pressure remained concentrated around the auctioned tenors.

## SpaceX Spreads Widen; Braskem Turns to the Courts

SpaceX's bonds weakened in secondary trading two days after its $25 billion debut. The 10-year notes traded at 157 basis points over Treasuries, 17 wider than their 140-basis-point issue spread. The new price showed that completing the jumbo sale had not exhausted investors' concerns about the issuer's spending and long path to free cash generation.

Dealers also began actively quoting five-year SpaceX credit-default swaps. One indication put the midpoint at 125.5 basis points annually, about $125,500 a year to protect $10 million of debt, versus roughly 64 basis points for similarly rated Intel. Capital intensity, concentrated governance and the future funding program were drawing a premium even with investment-grade ratings and substantial liquidity. The CDS quote was one market indication, alongside the more directly observed widening of the cash bonds.

Braskem moved from difficult negotiations to a request for emergency court protection after creditors rejected an out-of-court plan for longer maturities, lower coupons and grace periods. It reported about $9.5 billion of financial debt and roughly $3.7 billion of debt service from July 2026 through December 2027. Its shares fell more than 10%. A completed restructuring was still ahead; shareholder support, collateral and creditor ranking would now be central to the legal process.

Another industrial borrower, Indonesia's Gunbuster Nickel Industry, entered a court-ordered temporary debt suspension amid ore shortages and weak nickel prices. Indonesia supplies more than 60% of global nickel after a buildout financed largely with Chinese capital and expertise. The smelter's proceedings showed the strain on an individual project within that dominant industry, with eventual recoveries still unresolved.

Strategy's perpetual preferred STRC traded near $75 against its $100 issue price as Bitcoin fell below $60,000 and buyers retreated. The security has no claim on the company's Bitcoin, no maturity and a dividend that the board may reduce or suspend. Strategy itself carries a B- rating. Its funding model for continued Bitcoin accumulation was becoming more expensive, with preferred holders exposed below conventional debt in the capital structure.

### Bank Funding and Ratings Take Different Directions

Yokohama Financial Group sold its first senior bond, a ¥12 billion three-year issue at 27 basis points over JGBs. Final orders were about 1.2 times the offering, with life insurers, investment advisers and trust banks among buyers. The BOJ's increase to 1% had intensified deposit competition, encouraging regional banks with continuing loan demand to add wholesale funding. The debut secured that channel, though the book was modest.

China's regulators asked rating firms to examine the concentration of top grades and made issuance spreads over comparable government bonds one assessment measure. An issuer trading more than 200 basis points over the benchmark could risk losing AAA status, subject to other factors. At the end of the first quarter, 27% of more than 6,000 issuers were AAA and another 32% AA+. A wider distribution of ratings would give investors more differentiation and could raise costs for some borrowers accustomed to the top domestic label.

In the US, the FDIC proposed raising an asset threshold in part of its assessment framework to $30 billion from $10 billion. The Deposit Insurance Fund's reserve ratio stood at 1.43%, above the 1.35% statutory minimum and its highest in decades. Lower assessments could improve affected banks' retained earnings at the margin; the proposal remained subject to completion and did not alter the fund's obligation to absorb losses.

Broad credit returns were small beside those issuer developments. LQD rose 0.08%, HYG 0.04% and JNK 0.09%. Secondary spreads, legal status and capital structure conveyed more about the day's credit risks than the near-flat fund returns.

## Japan's Long-Bond Demand Weakens as Its Investment Plans Grow

Japan's 20-year auction drew 2.97 times the amount offered, the weakest coverage since May 2025 and below the 12-month average. The tail was the widest since January, and the lowest accepted price was well below the pre-sale estimate. Banks appeared to supply much of the demand as insurers and global managers reduced super-long JGB exposure. The result followed insurers' May selling and raised concern about renewed curve steepening.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's strategy added a large prospective financing question. It seeks more than ¥370 trillion, or $2.3 trillion, of public and private investment over 14 years in areas including AI and semiconductors. Government projections assume around ¥10 trillion of annual fiscal spending, with possible bridging bonds, tax revenue and spending savings in the funding mix. The full investment target is not all public debt, but issuance and a temporary increase in the debt ratio could precede the projected growth benefits.

BOJ board member Naoki Tamura described quarter-point increases every few months toward neutral near 2% as his baseline, following the previous week's move to 1%. Governor Kazuo Ueda again made further action dependent on growth and inflation. A persistently weak yen kept imported-price risks in view. The combination of weak long-bond bidding, possible supply and further policy increases gave domestic investors several reasons to reassess duration.

Tokyo CPI arrived later, at 8:30 JST on June 26, after the New York close. Prices excluding fresh food rose 1.6% from a year earlier, and the measure also excluding energy increased 1.9%. The key gauge accelerated for the first time in eight months, led by water-service fees after subsidies expired. That report updates the next Asian session's inflation outlook; the auction and policy news had already shaped Thursday's trading.

Europe's outlook had become less forceful after oil's earlier decline. Oxford Economics dropped its forecast for another ECB increase following June's move, and other forecasters reduced the number of steps they expected. Markets still priced a quarter-point increase this year. Isabel Schnabel and Emmanuel Moulin retained inflation vigilance, although Moulin called the recent increase moderate and noted that oil was below the assumptions in the latest forecasts. The debate was moving toward how long the ECB could pause.

UK 10-year gilt yields had fallen to around 4.7%, their lowest since mid-March, and broad gilt returns reached a three-month high despite political uncertainty. Lower imported energy costs had helped that recovery. Thursday's oil rebound put some of the support at risk without erasing the preceding decline in crude.

China introduced a new overnight reverse-repo instrument alongside its seven-day benchmark, held at 1.4% since May 2025. The PBOC gained a more direct way to manage overnight funding and limit money-market volatility. Traders read an easing bias into the change as second-quarter momentum weakened, a different direction from Japan's continued normalization.

## Oil Exporters Lose Support While China Markets Euro Debt

African oil exporters' dollar bonds had lagged the broader market during crude's June decline. Republic of Congo eurobonds lost more than 2%, and Angola, Cameroon, Gabon and Nigeria more than 1%, against an average EM gain of 0.5%. Angola's 2048 yield rose more than 60 basis points from its early-June low to 9.94%; Congo's 2036 yield climbed about 66 to 10.01%, and Nigeria's 2034 rose 33 to 7.33%.

Weak Chinese demand pushed some Angolan crude grades to their lowest prices in more than a decade and reduced interest in Congolese oil. Nigeria held up better because the Dangote refinery supplied domestic demand and earlier currency-market reforms had improved resilience. Thursday's security premium helped oil prices, but the large monthly losses still weighed on exporters' revenue and financing prospects.

China's Ministry of Finance was marketing up to €5 billion of five-, eight- and 12-year bonds at initial guidance of 15, 22 and 33 basis points over mid-swaps. It could become the country's largest euro sovereign sale, seven months after a €4 billion offering drew more than €100 billion of demand. The return sought favorable funding before possible European inflation and rate pressure. Those were marketing terms, with final pricing still to come.

China also called for legal and technical measures to curb aggressive bondholder litigation under the G20 Common Framework. Investors had begun suing Ethiopia over $1 billion of defaulted notes after failing to reach terms acceptable to their group and official creditors co-led by China. The dispute left burden sharing, enforcement and preferred-creditor treatment at the center of negotiations; official relief had not yet produced a durable private-creditor settlement.

Hungary's convergence story drew a different response. Its 10-year yield fell to 5.16%, within half a percentage point of UK debt after a 2.6-percentage-point premium in March. The spread over Germany narrowed to 2.3 percentage points, about half its level three months earlier. Access to more than €16 billion of previously frozen EU aid and a pledge to meet euro-entry criteria by 2030 supported the move despite Hungary's lower rating.

Philippine 10-year yields had fallen about 50 basis points since the June 15 US-Iran interim agreement, the strongest recovery in emerging Asia, after rising 157 basis points during the escalation through June 12. The BSP had raised its rate to 4.75% and its 2026 inflation forecast to 6.4%, above the 2%-4% target. One forecast called for three further quarter-point increases to 5.50%. The rebound thus remained exposed to inflation, the peso and El Niño-related supply risks.

Indonesia added controversial protections to attract funding for Danantara, which manages about $900 billion of state assets. A new financial-sector law shielded purchases of its bonds from criminal, civil and tax investigation and barred bond records from tax assessments or court evidence. With tax revenue around 10% of GDP, the measure could bring back undeclared capital and fund projects outside the headline deficit. It also reduced traceability, raising governance and reputational questions for investors.

Banxico held at 6.50% and signaled a longer pause despite Mexico's softer headline inflation and weak growth. GDP had contracted 0.6% in the first quarter, and the 2026 forecast had been cut to 1.1% from 1.6%. Persistent core inflation and sensitivity to US policy kept upside price risks in the board's assessment. The peso was stable after the decision. Across EM dollar bonds, EMB slipped just 0.01%, while the dollar's small daily decline eased immediate pressure without reversing its monthly advance.

## Chips Recover as the Hormuz Incident Lifts Oil

Micron's outlook revived confidence in AI hardware, helping the semiconductor index rise 3.59% and the Nasdaq 100 gain 0.75%. The S&P 500 was almost unchanged, down 0.01%, as Apple fell 6.1% after raising prices on Macs, iPads and home devices. VIX rose 1.40% to 18.89. The market's strong and weak points remained concentrated rather than moving together.

That concentration had become substantial. Eight infrastructure-linked stocks supplied almost two-thirds of the S&P 500's 7.5% year-to-date gain through Wednesday. Semiconductors were still about 93% higher for 2026 despite Tuesday's 7.9% loss. A small number of companies' investment and financing decisions therefore carried unusual weight in the broader market.

WTI reversed an early decline to finish 2.25% higher at $71.92, and Brent gained 2.06% to $75.26 after the vessel strike. Both had traded near prewar levels before the incident and were still about 6% lower over a week. Monthly losses exceeded 25% for WTI and 27% for Brent. The rebound restored some geopolitical premium to oil, consistent with the rise in Treasury breakevens, while leaving much of the previous energy relief intact.

The dollar index eased 0.18% to 101.43 but remained 0.58% higher over a week and 2.12% over a month. Gold gained 1.01% to $4,030.50, still down 4.58% over a week and 10.85% over a month. Gold and oil responded to renewed shipping uncertainty while bond investors retained some of the morning's real-yield gains.

## Inflation Expectations and Quarter-End Supply Come Next

The final University of Michigan survey and New York Fed Multivariate Core Trend Inflation measure are due June 26 at 10:00 ET. Michigan's preliminary readings were 48.9 for sentiment, 4.6% for one-year inflation expectations and 3.4% for longer-run expectations. The updates will put a measure of persistent price pressure beside Thursday's better-than-feared PCE release and the oil rebound.

Japan sells about ¥4.1 trillion of three-month bills around 12:35 JST on June 26, roughly ¥2.8 trillion of two-year JGBs June 30 and about ¥2.6 trillion of new 10-year bonds July 2. Those auctions will show whether weak demand is concentrated in super-long maturities. June 30 activity releases and the July 1 Tankan will also update investment and price expectations behind the BOJ's next steps.

US quarter-end supply begins with $92 billion of 13-week and $79 billion of 26-week bills on June 29 for July 2 settlement, then an $80 billion six-week sale June 30. June payrolls and weekly claims arrive July 2 at 8:30 ET, followed by four- and eight-week bill auctions at 11:30. Fixed-income trading is scheduled to close early at 14:00. Auction participation, cash-bill yields and the labor data will be available before the shortened session ends, with less trading time to absorb a surprise.

watch_events.market_implication: A dense calendar leaves less trading time to absorb labor-market or funding surprises.
watch_events.market_trigger: Track bill participation and cash yields before July 2's 08:30 ET data, 11:30 auctions and 14:00 fixed-income close.
watch_events.title: Quarter-end funding and the early close
watch_events.watch_line: $92 billion of 13-week and $79 billion of 26-week bills precede an $80 billion six-week sale; July 2 brings payrolls and claims.
